conventions.convention: The effective line model is an additional adopted model, with state space L²(R; C) of almost-everywhere classes and inner product linear in the first argument. Its one-dimensional reduction is not derived from P5.
The Fourier transform uses exp(-2πixξ); consequently c = 2π²ℏ²/m and H₀ = -(ℏ²/2m)D² on W²,²(R; C).

A bound state means a unit eigenvector with E < 0 relative to the declared zero reference; signed binding energy is E and its positive magnitude is -E. No general spectral threshold is inferred for arbitrary bounded V.

Generalized stationary solutions are bounded C¹ functions, piecewise C² solutions of the stationary equation; they need not be L² preparations. The scattering theorem uses incident amplitude 1 m⁻¹ᐟ² and reads T and R as current ratios, without assigning Born probabilities or particle counts to these solutions.

Robin conditions use coordinate derivatives u′(0) = αu(0) and u′(L) = βu(L), with both parameters in m⁻¹. Delta coupling uses u′(0+) - u′(0-) = (2mg/ℏ²)u(0), with g in J m; its second-derivative action is taken separately on the two half-lines.
Interval eigenvalues and sine eigenfunctions start at n = 1. Finite-well branches start at n = 0, with admissibility nπ/(2a) < K strictly; equality does not add a zero-energy bound state.

load_bearing.statement: For real bounded measurable V, the assigned line-model energy operator is H_V = H₀ˡⁱⁿ + M_V on D(H_V) = W²,²(R; C), acting as -(ℏ²/2m)D² + V; the definition also fixes bound-state and generalized-stationary-solution vocabulary.

Under Countable Choice and Choice, for self-adjoint A on a nonzero complex Hilbert space and real c > 0, cA on D(A) is self-adjoint; ρ(cA) = cρ(A), σ(cA) = cσ(A), and (cA-z)⁻¹ = c⁻¹(A-z/c)⁻¹. Compact resolvents and eigenfamilies transfer as stated, eigenspaces correspond exactly, and quadratic-form lower bounds scale by c.

Under Countable Choice and Choice, the free operator with Fourier multiplier (2π²ℏ²/m)|ξ|² has domain W²,²(R; C) and equals -(ℏ²/2m)D² there. Adding a real bounded measurable V gives the same-domain weak differential operator and equivalent eigenvalue equation.

The interval energy operators are -(ℏ²/2m)D² + V on the displayed Dirichlet or separated Robin H² domains. The zero-range model is H_g = (ℏ²/2m)A_(2mg/ℏ²), on the H¹(R), piecewise-H² interface domain with the declared derivative jump.

For a > 0 and U > E > 0, the declared barrier has a unique scattering solution with prescribed incident reference amplitude and transmission asymptotics. T = [1 + U²sinh²(κa)/(4E(U-E))]⁻¹, R = 1-T, and the current is conserved. With q = exp(-2κa), C = U²/(4E(U-E)), and δ = (4/C-2)q + q², T = (4/C)q/(1+δ), with the stated error bound whenever |δ| ≤ 1/2.

For the declared well of depth U > 0 and half-width a > 0, all eigenvalues lie in (-U,0), are simple, and satisfy k tan(ka) = κ or -k cot(ka) = κ. Their number is ceil(2aK/π), with exactly one root in each admissible branch whose left endpoint is strictly below K, alternating even and odd types.

For the declared Dirichlet and Robin interval models with real continuous V, the energy operators are self-adjoint with compact resolvent and complete simple eigenbases. Dirichlet eigenfunction n has n-1 interior zeros and |ℰ_n-ℏ²π²n²/(2mL²)| ≤ ||V||∞; the free eigenfunctions are sqrt(2/L) sin(nπx/L). The Robin eigenvalue condition is β = u_a′(L,λ_n)/u_a(L,λ_n), with nonzero denominator.

concerns.concern: Proof step 1.1 says 'by [F1] a class u ... has a second weak derivative in L² exactly when' its quadratic Fourier multiplier is in L². F1 and its cited lemma state the forward implication for an already existing L² weak derivative, not this converse. The domain equality is independently available from F2, and the converse can be justified through the Fourier/Sobolev supplier or an inverse-transform test-function argument; the present attribution is stronger than its cited statement.

The YAML title contains the TeX-style escaped spelling Schr\"odinger in prose. YAML decodes this to Schr"odinger, rather than Schrödinger, as also reflected in the assigned inventory title. This is a title-spelling defect.

Proof step 2.2 calls the compact-resolvent transfer 'the general statement of [F5]'. F5 explicitly assumes a compact resolvent at a real point, whereas the Robin Green-resolvent supplier directly constructs nonreal resolvents. F6 already supplies the required general positive-scaling transfer, so the conclusion is supported, but this attribution should not suggest F5 has a hypothesis-free arbitrary-resolvent statement.

seams_checked.note: Contextual page-order prerequisite. The batch proves its own one-dimensional flux identity and does not import a three-dimensional detector or finite-sampling conclusion.
Uses the free Fourier operator and bounded real-potential theorem with d=1 and c=2π²ℏ²/m; preserves its domain and bounded-potential restriction.

Preserves continuous interval potentials, Robin signs, delta interface domain, barrier restriction U>E>0, and strict finite-well thresholds. Arbitrary endpoint well values are explicitly removed by almost-everywhere operator equality.
Postulates remain adopted assumptions; units, choice hypotheses and apparatus qualifications are retained. No measured parameter is asserted.
Uses the spin-zero baseline as context and explicitly adopts, rather than derives, its effective one-dimensional reduction and position-law reading.
Uses domain-sensitive self-adjoint assigned observables and eigenvalue atoms. Generalized scattering solutions are excluded from normalized Born preparation laws.
Preserves U(t)=exp(-itH/ℏ), the energy-domain differentiability condition, stationary-ray equivalence and bounded energy-compatible observable qualifications.
Uses the abstract diagonal-domain lemma for the sine family, with harmless reindexing from n=0 to n=1; does not apply an oscillator differential realization to the box.
Examples preserve the declared dimensional parameters and current reference amplitude; exact computations are not presented as observations.
The box uses the normalized complete sine family on (0,L), starting at n=1; its nodal points exclude endpoints.

Coulomb consumers use only the general positive-scaling lemma for domains, self-adjointness, spectra and eigenspaces. Spectral-PVM scaling is separately supplied; no bounded-line-potential theorem is applied to Coulomb.
The WKB definition explicitly takes V in C_c⁵(R; R), hence within the bounded measurable line model, and separately states its classical stationary equation and approximation assumptions.

The smooth/rectangular comparison quotes the exact rectangular formula and dimensionless amplitude ratio with U>E>0; it distinguishes the rectangular thick-width prefactor from the smooth semiclassical limit.

The scaling-correspondence lemma uses the abstract positive-scaling statements with the nonzero Hilbert-space hypothesis. The Dollard consumer obtains additional PVM/subspace correspondence from separately cited spectral calculus, without claiming it is contained in the scaling lemma alone.
